## ✨ Highlights

- 🔗 **A cluster's members say so**: a member's page names its cluster - and its VRRP role -, the Nodes page frames a cluster's members together, and what the cluster manages is no longer offered for editing on a member's page: the page says why, with an emergency release for an admin ([locks and drift](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md#locks-and-drift)).
- ⚙️ **Settings**: how often the nodes and the hypervisors are asked, the nodes' figures and their charts (off: not sampled at all), times in UTC or in the browser's zone, traffic in bits or in bytes - kept with each account on the Controller; refresh floors for an admin; the HTTPS certificate moved there.
- 📈 **Watching clusters**: the Controller's metrics say each member's version, drift and failures; nine alerts and a Grafana dashboard, **Janus · Clusters** ([metrics](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/metrics.md)).
- 🌊 **A Traffic flow that tells the truth, and moves smoothly**: HAProxy's and the interfaces' rates over the same 10 s, each figure saying what it counts, and dots that never restart at a refresh - they fade out and back in.
- 🧾 **Logs name their cluster**: Elasticsearch documents and RFC 5424 syslog messages carry the member's cluster.

## 🔗 Clusters

- **On a member's page** ([#334](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/334)): the top bar names the cluster and the member - a link to the cluster's page on the Controller -, with the member's VRRP role when the cluster manages VRRP, and "drained". What the cluster manages there - HAProxy's configuration and going back in its history, files, certificates, VRRP, BGP, the firewall's ruleset - is no longer offered: the node refused it anyway. Those pages say why, link the cluster, and offer an admin **Release this node's lock…** for an emergency change - drift the cluster reports, and its next apply takes back.
- **On the Nodes page**: a cluster's members framed under its heading - its name, its members, the version they run against the one it wants, its health -, as cards and in the list; the other nodes after.
- **Logs** ([#333](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/333), [log forwarding](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/log-forwarding.md)): a member's records carry its cluster - `orchestrator.cluster.name`, `orchestrator.cluster.id`, `orchestrator.type: janus` and `janus.cluster.member` in Elasticsearch, `[janus@32473 cluster_id cluster_name member]` structured data in RFC 5424 syslog -, read when they're sent: a filter shows a whole cluster. RFC 3164 messages and a node in no cluster are unchanged; an Elasticsearch document's `_id` too.

## 📈 Watching clusters

- **The Controller's metrics** ([#335](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/335)): `janus_cluster_desired_version`, `janus_cluster_operation_failed`, and per member `janus_cluster_member_applied_version`, `_on_desired_version`, `_drift{domain}`, `_released{domain}`, `_error`, `_drained`, `_peers`, `_peers_up`, `_tables_synced`, `_checked_timestamp_seconds` - on `GET /api/metrics`, a reader token.
- **Alerts**: a `janus-clusters` group in `examples/prometheus/janus-rules.yml` - a VRRP instance with no master among a cluster's members or more than one, a peer down, a stick table not synced, a member drifted, not on the desired version or failing, an operation failed or running too long -, each naming the cluster and the member, tested with `promtool test rules`.
- **A Grafana dashboard, Janus · Clusters** (`grafana/janus-clusters.json`): one cluster at a time - its members, who holds the virtual address and its failovers, peers and stick tables, each member's traffic and load, and the Controller's view of it; checked on Grafana 11.6, 12.0 and 13.0.

## 🖥️ Controller

- **Settings** ([#336](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/336)), every account's: nodes refreshed every 5 s to 1 min, hypervisors every 10 s to 2 min (3 s while a machine moves); the **node figures** - off, the Nodes page asks for none, and the Controller stops sampling the nodes for it - and their **charts** - off, the figures alone, and a node's Traffic flow without its dots; **times** in the browser's zone or in UTC - every time shown, a node's pages too, says "UTC" when it is; **traffic** in bytes (KiB/s) or bits (Mbit/s) a second; reset to the defaults. Kept with the account on the Controller (`/api/me/preferences`): they follow it to any browser. For an admin, **refresh floors** - the shortest refresh any account may choose - and the **HTTPS certificate**, moved from the Nodes page.
- **Hypervisors and machines as cards or a list**, each list its own choice, remembered per browser.
- **Enrollment tokens** stay with the nodes' provisioning, now linked from **Add a node** and from the API tokens page.
- **A node's trust error stays in its card**: a short badge, the message wrapped below it - three lines at most, the whole of it in the tooltip.

## 🌊 Traffic flow

- **Why eth0 read 42 MiB/s while the frontends summed to 450 KiB/s** ([#337](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/337)): eth0 carries every proxied byte twice - from the server, to the client -, and HAProxy adds a connection's bytes to its counters only when the connection ends, unless `option contstats` (every 5 s): a TCP relay's long-lived sessions barely showed. The page now averages HAProxy's and the interfaces' counters over the same 10 s, a counter reset or a gap gives no spike, each figure says what it counts, and a TCP frontend without `contstats` is marked ([live traffic: option contstats](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/haproxy-config.md)).
- **Its dots no longer restart at every refresh**: made once, their speed eased without restarting them; at 0 they wait a moment, then fade out in 0.3 s, and fade back in when traffic resumes. Still under "reduce motion", and when the account's node charts are off.

- `ui-preview`'s browser check: a member's badge and locks, a cluster's members framed on the Nodes page; Settings - no metrics request with the figures off, no curve with the charts off, the refresh followed, a floor, traffic in bit/s, a node's events in UTC; a long trust error at 360 px; the hypervisors and machines as lists.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Syslog receivers**: a cluster member's RFC 5424 messages now carry structured data (`[janus@32473 …]`) instead of `-`. 32473 is IANA's documentation number - the SD-ID may change once Janus has its own.
- **`option contstats`** in a `defaults` section used by long-lived TCP frontends makes their live rates true - HAProxy's own counting, nothing Janus sets for you.
- **The Controller's new metrics** need it scraped with a reader API token (job `janus-controller` in the docs' example).
